text: Welcome back to the fourth and final module of the course.
In this module, we'll cover the underlying principles of large-scale graph processing
and the software infrastructure that supports it.
So in this module, you'll learn a programming model for graph computation
and systems that implement this model.
After this module, you'll be able to formulate graph analytics computations
in terms of the programming model.
This module will consist of three lessons.
The first lesson will revisit the concept of a programming model
and introduce a programming model called Bulk Synchronous Parallel, or BSP,
that is designed specifically for graph-oriented computation.
I will discuss two well-known versions of the central idea,
Bregel from Google and GraphLab from Carnegie Mellon University.
The second lesson will discuss two software systems,
Giraffe that operates on Hadoop and GraphX that operates on Spark.
We'll compare the basic architecture of these two systems and point out their differences.
The final lesson will show example computations using the GraphX platform.
Since GraphX comes with Spark, we have created these examples on the virtual machine which you have access to.
The code and some datasets are available for those who wish to play with the system.
